skip_reason: Existing-move logistics only — not a sales call. This is an outbound pre-move confirmation call on an already-booked job: Chauny opens with 'I was just calling in regards to your move on the 8th of September. Do you have a moment to kind of run through some details with me?' The move date, the origin and destination addresses, the home sizes, and the arrival window (8:15-8:45) are all already on file and she is reading them back for verification. The customer had already received a written quote ($855) before the call. There is no quote being built, no pricing pitch, no differentiator pitch, no clock explanation, and no booking attempt, because the booking already exists. The only pricing content is Chauny narrowing the already-delivered estimate to a $647-$855 range based on the verified inventory, which is estimate refinement on a booked job rather than an estimate presentation. Grading this against the 9-section sales scorecard would produce a misleadingly low number and pollute the run average.
top_strength: Not graded (skip). Worth noting for the record: this is a genuinely useful verification call. Chauny pulled real inventory detail the file did not have (two dressers, a full bed that disassembles, a 55-inch TV, TV stands, a futon, desks) and caught that the customer is self-moving two PCs. She also corrected a destination address the system had wrong, taking the customer's 'Avalon Tech Ridge' over the mapped 'John Henry / Fluke' entry and adding a note because 'Google likes to do their own thing' — that is exactly the kind of catch that protects drive time on move day.
coaching_note: Not graded (skip). Two non-scorecard observations for Amanda. First, the estimate-accuracy angle: Chauny revised a booked $855 quote down to a $647-$855 range on the call, telling the customer 'this move seems pretty straightforward so we're keeping you all in that minimal range.' That is a verbal re-anchor to the bottom of the range on a two-story-stairs-both-ends move, and if the actual lands near $855 the customer will experience it as an overage — relevant to the estimate-accuracy rock, and worth checking whether the revised range was written back into EMMA. Second, the customer volunteered a real access concern (tight parking at the Georgetown origin, with prior move-in problems) and got 'I'm sure they'll figure it out, they're professional' before Chauny noted it. She did note it, but the reassurance landed ahead of the acknowledgment; better is naming it back first — 'tight turn at the Georgetown entrance, prior move had issues, I'm flagging it for the crew.' This call also had no Save Your Ass prep speech, which is in scope even on a confirmation call and is the single highest-leverage thing a pre-move call can add, since prep is the lever that keeps this job in the minimum range she just promised.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and light without sounding scripted — 'Doing amazing, it's Friday' as an opener, repeated genuine thanks for information ('No, thank you for that information, I do appreciate it'), Jonathan's name used at open and close, and a warm sign-off ('Have a great weekend') that the customer met with 'Sweet, thank you so much'; held back from a 5 by heavy reliance on 'perfect/alright/okay' as filler and by smoothing past the parking concern rather than sitting with it.
